adjudication_records.issue_text: Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts uses computed keys like [z.string().toString()] that evaluate to junk instead of validating any numeric field as expiry and allowing other properties, so payloads missing expiry pass validation and tokens are treated as always-expired

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to use computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JS these evaluate to a single fixed string key (e.g. `"[object Object]"`), not a wildcard, so the schema does *not* validate “any numeric field as expiry” nor “allow other properties” as intended. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, `safeParse` will likely fail for normal token payloads (e.g. ones with `expiry_date`/`expires_in`) and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` will throw `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned`. The finding’s specific claim about missing expiry *passing* validation/always-expired isn’t shown, but the schema issue itself is a real defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts webhook performs unguarded JSON.parse on symmetricDecrypt output with no schema validation before writing to credential.key, so malformed payloads crash with 500 or invalid JSON is persisted as credential key

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""));` with no try/catch and no zod/schema validation of the decrypted payload before persisting it via `prisma.credential.update/create({ data: { key: keys, ... }})`. If `symmetricDecrypt` returns non-JSON (wrong key, malformed ciphertext, attacker input), `JSON.parse` will throw and the route will error (500) rather than returning a controlled 4xx. Also, even when JSON parses, arbitrary JSON shape is written into `credential.key` without validation, which can lead to invalid credential data being stored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sync fetch in refreshOAuthTokens.ts has no response.ok check, no Content-Type JSON header, no timeout, and no auth, so a 500 from the credential sync endpoint is passed through as a successful response

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sync is enabled it does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and returns the raw `Response` without checking `response.ok` or otherwise handling non-2xx statuses. Multiple callers treat the return value as a successful token payload/axios-like response (e.g. GoogleCalendarService uses `const token = res?.data;` and then reads `token.access_token`, Hubspot assigns the result to `HubspotToken`), so a 500 (or any non-OK) response from the sync endpoint can propagate and lead to incorrect behavior/crashes rather than being rejected/handled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:17-19 fabricates a literal 'refresh_token' placeholder string when the sync response omits a refresh token, which will fail when sent to the provider

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, after parsing a token refresh response it unconditionally sets `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token" when missing (`if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`). Several callers then merge `tokenResponse.data` into stored credentials (e.g. `Office365CalendarService` spreads `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` and writes it back to Prisma), which can overwrite a previously valid `refresh_token` with this bogus placeholder. That can later break refresh flows whenever the real refresh token is needed (e.g., if sync is turned off, or any code path falls back to provider refresh).

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-9 uses computed keys from .toString() on Zod instances, producing non-dynamic literal keys so minimumTokenResponseSchema is non-functional dead logic that silently loosens validation

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately, producing a fixed literal property name (whatever the ZodString instance’s `toString()` returns), not a dynamic/index-signature. As a result, the schema does not validate “any numeric expiry field” nor “any other fields”; instead it defines one (required) numeric property with that literal name, making the schema incorrect and likely to fail `safeParse` for real token responses. This is a verifiable functional defect in the new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService.ts:75-99 has a bespoke refresh flow that is neither gated by the feature flag nor routed through refreshOAuthTokens, causing unconditional fetch to Salesforce token endpoint and credential overwrite even with sync disabled

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh logic performs a direct `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` without using the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper or checking `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`/`CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. The diff shows other integrations were updated to route refreshes through `refreshOAuthTokens` to support the credential-sync mode; Salesforce was not, so it will never use the sync endpoint when that mode is enabled. However, the finding’s implication that refreshing/updating “even with sync disabled” is inherently a defect is not verifiable from the diff (other integrations also refresh/update when sync is disabled via the fallback path).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce refresh flow uses fragile response.statusText !== 'OK' check instead of proper 2xx status check
matched_golden_ids: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same core bug: the Salesforce OAuth token refresh handler relies on `response.statusText` (e.g., comparing to 'OK') rather than using `response.ok`/2xx status semantics, which is brittle and can misclassify successful responses, leading to refresh failures and stale credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 replaces appConfig.slug with hardcoded 'zoho-bigin' in the redirect URI, unrelated scope drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts` changing the redirect URI from using `appConfig.slug` to a hardcoded `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback`. This is a real, reviewable concern because it reduces configurability/consistency with the config-driven slug and is not directly tied to the OAuth utils refactor/credential sync changes, but it is not a clearly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone (it may be equivalent if `appConfig.slug` is already `zoho-bigin`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse validation is only applied to 4 of 8 modified apps, leaving hubspot/lark/webex/zoho synced responses unvalidated before being persisted via prisma.credential.update

adjudication.rationale: While the diff does show `parseRefreshTokenResponse` being introduced and only used in a subset of integrations (e.g., googlecalendar, office365calendar, salesforce, zoomvideo), the finding’s specific claim that hubspot/lark/webex/zoho “leave synced responses unvalidated before being persisted via prisma.credential.update” is not verifiable from the shown hunks. The diff excerpts for hubspot/lark/webex/zoho only show swapping token-refresh calls to `refreshOAuthTokens`; they do not show a `prisma.credential.update` that persists the (potentially synced) refresh response without validation. Also, the “4 of 8 modified apps” framing doesn’t match what’s clearly shown (more than 8 apps are touched).

adjudication_records.issue_text: hubspot casts refreshOAuthTokens result to HubspotToken though in sync mode it returns a raw fetch Response, so the type is misleading

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `hubspotRefreshToken` is typed as `HubspotToken` but is assigned from `await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the “sync mode” branch returns the raw `fetch(...)` result (a `Response`), not a parsed token object. So when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Hubspot will receive a `Response` where downstream code expects `HubspotToken`, causing runtime breakage; the type annotation is therefore misleading and the behavior is incorrect in that mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED flag doesn't account for CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, allowing the feature to be partially enabled in a half-working state

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is intentionally defined as the presence of `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts). The other env vars are already treated as optional/independent: `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` has a default fallback (`|| "calcom-webhook-secret"`) in the webhook handler, and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is separately checked in `refreshOAuthTokens`/`parseRefreshTokenResponse` before using the sync behavior. So the code does not enter a “half-working” broken state; it cleanly falls back when optional vars are absent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse silently fabricates a fake refresh_token value, and in Google Calendar the result is written to prisma.credential.update, permanently destroying the user's real refresh token

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `parseRefreshTokenResponse` mutates parsed data to add `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing, and it returns the *safeParse result object* (with `.success`/`.data`), not the parsed `.data` itself. In Google Calendar refresh, the code changed from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...); await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, which will persist that wrapper object into `credential.key` instead of the credential payload. That is a verifiable corruption/data-loss bug (subsequent code expecting `credential.key.refresh_token` etc. will break). The finding’s specific claim that a fabricated refresh_token overwrites the real one in Google is not directly shown (Google passes an object that likely still contains the original refresh_token), but persisting the wrong structure is still a concrete defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens sync branch returns a raw fetch Response while Hubspot, Zoho Bigin, and ZohoCRM adapters expect an axios/SDK response object, causing tokenInfo.data to be undefined and a runtime crash

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch(...)` directly in the sync branch (`return response;`), which is a WHATWG `Response` object (no `.data`). Several callers expect an axios/SDK-style response: e.g. Zoho Bigin uses `tokenInfo.data.error` and ZohoCRM uses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`, which will be `undefined` and can crash at runtime when credential sync is enabled. Hubspot similarly assigns the return value to `HubspotToken`, but would receive a `Response` in the sync branch, breaking downstream property access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService now performs an eager, unconditional token refresh on every service instantiation even when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is false, burning Salesforce rate limits

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, after `const credentialKey = credential.key as ...`, the code now always calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and updates the stored credential before creating the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no conditional check around this refresh (e.g., no `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` gating), so the refresh happens on every service construction regardless of that flag. This is a concrete, diff-grounded concern about unnecessary token refresh/rate-limit usage, but it’s not provably a correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce stored credential gets corrupted because parseRefreshTokenResponse stores only minimum-schema fields plus the fake 'refresh_token' value

adjudication.rationale: In the Salesforce refresh flow, the Prisma update explicitly preserves the original refresh token: `data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token } }` (packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts). So even though `parseRefreshTokenResponse` may inject a placeholder `refresh_token` when missing, Salesforce overwrites it with the existing real value, meaning the specific claim about a fake refresh_token corrupting the stored credential is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Office365 CalendarService deleted explicit logging of tokenResponse.error and the raw MS response on parse failure, making OAuth refresh errors opaque

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code changed from `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` followed by a `console.error(...)` when `!tokenResponse.success` to using `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, which throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on parse failure and no longer logs `tokenResponse.error` or the raw `responseJson`. This reduces diagnosability/observability of OAuth refresh failures but does not by itself constitute a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sync payload sends only calcomUserId and appSlug without the user's refresh_token or an Authorization header, risking persisting credentials for the wrong account over valid user credentials via the webhook handler

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s `refreshOAuthTokens` posts to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, but this code path does not invoke the new webhook handler at `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` at all. The webhook handler is a separate endpoint that requires a secret header and an encrypted `keys` payload, and nothing in the diff shows `refreshOAuthTokens` (or its callers) sending data to that webhook or causing credentials to be persisted via it. Therefore the stated risk of overwriting credentials “via the webhook handler” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricated 'refresh_token' placeholder string is persisted as a real credential, replacing the user's actual refresh token and permanently breaking the integration

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, the response is parsed with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (which does not require `refresh_token`), and then the function forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` if missing. This value is then spread into persisted credentials in at least `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };` followed by `prisma.credential.update(... data: { key: o365AuthCredentials } ...)`, which would overwrite the real refresh token with the placeholder string, breaking future refreshes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zod 'minimum' schema uses computed keys via z.string().toString() producing garbage keys, so it only validates access_token and bypasses strict per-provider schemas in sync mode

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to model arbitrary keys via computed properties `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions evaluate immediately to fixed string property names (e.g., a Zod schema’s `toString()`), not an index signature/catchall. As a result, the schema will require/define nonsensical literal keys rather than accepting real OAuth fields like `expires_in`, likely causing `safeParse` to fail (and token refresh to throw) whenever sync mode is enabled. The finding’s “bypasses strict schemas” rationale is a bit off, but the core defect (garbage computed keys making the minimum schema invalid) is directly grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Decrypted webhook payload is JSON.parse'd and stored as credential.key with no schema validation, allowing arbitrary structure injection

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted `reqBody.keys` is `JSON.parse`d and then written directly to `prisma.credential.update/create` as `key: keys` with no Zod/schema validation of the structure. This means any JSON object (once decrypted) can be persisted as `credential.key`, which can lead to malformed credential data and potential abuse if the webhook secret is compromised or misconfigured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time !== instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual, allowing timing observation

adjudication.rationale:
In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook secret is validated via a direct `!==` comparison:

```ts
req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
```

This is not a constant-time comparison. For secret-token validation, using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (after normalizing to buffers and handling length mismatch) is the standard mitigation against timing attacks. The diff directly introduces this potentially timing-leakable secret comparison in a network-exposed endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook header lookup can return string[] for duplicate headers, causing array !== string comparison to fail closed

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check does `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. In Next/Node, `req.headers[...]` can be `string | string[] | undefined` when a header is repeated. If it’s `string[]`, the strict comparison to the expected secret string will always fail, causing legitimate requests with duplicate headers to be rejected (fail-closed but still broken behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME silently falls back to a default header name instead of rejecting inconsistent config

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the header name used for secret verification is `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"`, so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is unset it silently falls back to the default. This matches the finding’s claim about fallback behavior. Whether it *should* reject inconsistent/missing config is a product/ops decision rather than a clear functional defect, but it is a real, diff-grounded configuration footgun (no validation/error when env var is missing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credential sync endpoint called with no authentication, no scheme enforcement, and its unauthenticated response is trusted as OAuth tokens

adjudication.rationale: The new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper will call `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) and sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the POST body, with no authentication headers/signature and no enforcement that the endpoint is HTTPS. Call sites then treat the response as the refreshed OAuth token source (e.g., Office365/Zoom parse it via `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, which even relaxes validation when credential sync is enabled and can synthesize a `refresh_token`). This matches the finding that an unauthenticated endpoint response is trusted as token material.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .env.example suggests 'openssl rand -base64 24' (24 bytes) despite comment requiring 32-byte AES-256 key, creating a deployment misconfiguration trap

adjudication.rationale: In `.env.example`, the new `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` block states the key "must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm" but suggests generating it with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which produces 24 random bytes (then base64-encoded), not 32 bytes. Given the code uses this env var for `symmetricDecrypt(...)` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, following the example can lead to runtime crypto failures/misconfiguration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new webhook endpoint apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts (secret check, decrypt, create-vs-update credential branching) has no corresponding tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new non-trivial Next.js API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` with auth/secret-header validation, zod parsing, decryption via `symmetricDecrypt`, and create-vs-update branching against Prisma credentials. The diff does not add any test files or test changes covering this new behavior (no additions under a test directory or similar), so within the PR diff there are no corresponding tests for the new endpoint logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts is a new function with a non-trivial branch (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT) and a refresh-token fallback mutation, untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new helper `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` with behavior that changes based on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (switching from the provided schema to `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)`) and it mutates the parsed data by setting `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token" when missing. This is non-trivial parsing/behavior used by multiple integrations (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom/Salesforce in the diff), and no corresponding tests are added/updated in the shown changes, making a targeted “needs tests/coverage for these branches and the refresh_token fallback” a concrete review concern tied to this diff rather than a generic request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts is a new function whose sync-enabled branch replaces every app's real token refresh with a fetch to an external endpoint, untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` and wires it into multiple integrations’ refresh paths (e.g., Google, Hubspot, Lark, O365, Zoom, Webex, Zoho). When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set and `userId` is present, the wrapper bypasses the integration-specific refresh logic and instead does a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, returning that response. This is a significant behavior/architecture change introducing an external dependency and a different contract (no status/error handling/auth here), but the claim that it’s “untested” isn’t directly verifiable from the diff (no tests shown either way).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99 adds eager token refresh plus prisma.credential.update inside service construction, untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an eager Salesforce token refresh and persists it immediately: in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, right after `const credentialKey = ...`, it performs a POST to Salesforce `/oauth2/token`, parses, and then `await prisma.credential.update(...)` before constructing/returning the `jsforce.Connection`. That introduces side effects (network + DB write) during service initialization and changes when refresh occurs (always on construction), which is a meaningful architectural/behavioral concern. However, the claim that this is "untested" is not verifiable from the diff alone (no test changes shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:4-9 uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()], which reduce to literal keys '[object String]'/'[object Undefined]', so the schema only ever validates access_token and tests against it are false-confidence tests by construction
matched_golden_ids: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same core bug: the Zod schema is built with computed property keys derived from `z.string().toString()` / `z.string().optional().toString()`, which is invalid/incorrect usage and results in nonsensical literal keys (e.g., `[object String]`), causing the schema not to behave as intended (and likely to fail at runtime or validate incorrectly).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The refresh_token = "refresh_token" sentinel fallback (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23) can write a placeholder string into the credential store for sync-mode responses of arbitrary/wrong shape

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when in sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the function parses via `minimumTokenResponseSchema` and then forcibly sets `refresh_token` to the literal string `"refresh_token"` if it’s missing (lines ~21-23). Call sites then persist/merge this into stored credentials; e.g. `Office365CalendarService` does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` and then updates Prisma, so the placeholder can overwrite the real refresh token and be written to the credential store. This is a concrete, diff-introduced correctness/data-loss issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts (Google): parseRefreshTokenResponse result object (SafeParseReturnType wrapper) is persisted as credential.key instead of parsed data, irreversibly destroying Google OAuth tokens

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.ts, `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` returns the full Zod `safeParse` result object (i.e., `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed token data. The diff shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` followed by `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, which would persist the wrapper object as `credential.key` instead of the OAuth credential payload. This would corrupt stored credentials (data-loss / broken refresh) compared to the prior `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returned the actual token object.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts: literal placeholder string 'refresh_token' is injected when response lacks refresh_token, which callers then persist over real refresh tokens (O365, Zoom, Salesforce)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when the parsed token data lacks `refresh_token`, it forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Call sites then merge/persist parsed data: e.g. Office365 (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`) and Zoom (replacing `safeParse` with `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) can overwrite an existing real refresh token with this literal placeholder if the provider omits `refresh_token` on refresh responses. The finding overstates Salesforce specifically: Salesforce explicitly re-adds the original `credentialKey.refresh_token` when persisting, so it won’t be clobbered there, but the underlying placeholder-token bug is still present and affects other callers shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService.ts: credential.key rebuilt solely from loosely-validated token response plus old refresh_token, dropping previously stored fields like instance_url, signature, id, issued_at

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the updated credential key is persisted as `key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }`. `accessTokenParsed` comes from `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)`, and that helper switches to a very loose `minimumTokenResponseSchema` whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set. In that mode, the parsed data may contain only `access_token` (and numeric expiry), so the DB update would drop previously stored Salesforce fields like `instance_url`, `id`, `issued_at`, `signature`, etc. Future uses of this credential (e.g., `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url`) would then break due to missing fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService.ts: refresh+persist now runs on every service construction instead of lazily, so a misbehaving sync endpoint corrupts all credentials immediately

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `SalesforceCalendarService` now unconditionally refreshes tokens from Salesforce (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token"...)`) and updates the Prisma credential immediately, but it does **not** call the new `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`/`refreshOAuthTokens` path. So the finding’s core claim that a “misbehaving sync endpoint corrupts all credentials” is not supported by the shown changes. Also, whether this runs on “every service construction” vs “lazily” can’t be verified from the snippet alone (we don’t see the constructor/call sites).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts webhook: overwrites existing credential's key with pushed keys without backup or versioning, and findFirst on {userId, appId} may pick the wrong credential when multiple exist

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, existing credentials are updated via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys } })`, which does overwrite the previous `key` with no in-code backup/versioning. Also, the lookup uses `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })`, so if multiple credentials could exist for the same `{userId, appId}` it would pick an arbitrary one; the diff does not show any uniqueness constraint or ordering to guarantee the intended record. This is a concrete, diff-grounded data-integrity/edge-case concern, but not a clearly provable defect without DB schema context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED env flag: enabling credential sync is a one-way cutover with no dual-write, backfill, or rollback path, overwriting provider-issued tokens

adjudication.rationale: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is active (derived from `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` + `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), token refresh paths switch to `refreshOAuthTokens()` and then validate via `parseRefreshTokenResponse()`. In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, the “minimum” schema is used and, because it is a plain `z.object(...)` without `.passthrough()`, it will strip unknown fields like `refresh_token` from the parsed result; the function then forcibly sets `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token" when absent. Call sites then persist this back to DB (e.g., Office365: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`, which will overwrite a real refresh token with the placeholder; Google/Zoom similarly feed parsed output into credential update). This is a verifiable data-loss/rollback-breaking behavior introduced by the diff (provider-issued refresh tokens can be overwritten with a dummy value once sync is enabled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts: 'allow other properties' schema is broken — z.string().toString() evaluates to literal key 'z.string()' not a wildcard, so extra properties are stripped and persisted key only contains access_token

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to model “any numeric expiry field” and “allow other properties” via computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()`. In a JS object literal this creates a single literal key (the result of `ZodString#toString()`, not a wildcard/index signature), so Zod will not accept arbitrary extra keys that way. With Zod objects defaulting to stripping unknown keys (and also requiring any explicitly declared keys), this schema will not behave as intended and will likely fail parsing unless the response contains that exact literal key. Correct approaches would be `.passthrough()`/`.catchall(...)` plus explicit known fields or a `z.record(...)` shape merged appropriately.
